messages:
inc-bot: Pager triggered: HIGH - gpu_vram_usage_spike (alert id: a-98324)
inc-bot: Nodes affected: prod-rt-03 prod-rt-04 prod-rt-05 prod-rt-06
Alex M: I'm on it. Observing a big tail-latency spike in the realtime inference pool. Can someone confirm customer-facing requests are impacted?
Maria G: Confirmed — we've got elevated 95th p50->p95 delta on /v1/generate in the EU region. A small subset of requests are timing out at 30s.
Lee (oncall): looks like VRAM on those nodes is ~97% and fragmentation metric is high. GPU thermal is ok. No ECC spikes yet.
jen_ops: I'm going to silence the per-node "gpu.vram.percent > 90" noisy alerts for prod-rt-0[3-6] for 20m while we triage. Using AlertManager: `curl -XPOST http://alertmanager/api/v1/silences -d '{"matchers":[{"name":"alertname","value":"gpu_vram_usage_spike","isRegex":false}],"startsAt":"2026-03-15T15:00:00Z","endsAt":"2026-03-15T15:20:00Z","createdBy":"jen_ops","comment":"temp mute while investigating fragmentation"}'`
Samir: +1 on silencing — alert noise is drowning other signals. But let's not just mute: need rule change.
Alex M: Agreed. Initial mitigation: drain non-critical batch jobs off prod-rt-05/06, bump realtime routing away from 05. Can someone trigger k8s drain and update LB weights?
jen_ops: Running `kubectl drain prod-rt-05 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` now. Will shift traffic by reducing replicas in deployment realtime-api-eu from 12->8 on those nodes.
Maria G: On the monitoring side I propose changing the alert to only page at severity=page if `avg_over_time(gpu_memory_used_bytes/gpu_memory_total_bytes[3m]) > 0.92` and also add a fragmentation gate `gpu_vram_fragmentation_ratio > 0.7` to reduce false positives from transient peaks.
Lee (oncall): Also suggest adding a cadence rule: if same node fires >3 times in 30m escalate to page, otherwise lower to warning. Prevents flapping.
Samir: This is where we can use adaptive rules. New proposed Prometheus rule (draft):
```
- alert: gpu_vram_high_sustained
  expr: avg_over_time(gpu_memory_used_bytes/gpu_memory_total_bytes[3m]) > 0.92 and gpu_vram_fragmentation_ratio > 0.7
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Sustained GPU VRAM pressure on {{ $labels.instance }}"
```

Alex M: Nice. Can we also correlate with `gpu_ecc_corrected_total` and `node_temp_celsius` on the dashboard so the oncall can triage faster? If ECC rises we escalate to hardware team.
jen_ops: I'll add a temporary panel to the incident dashboard linking VRAM, fragmentation, ECC correcteds, and current running pods (by mem_request).
Maria G: FYI customers affected: 2 enterprise customers in EU had increased error rates during the spike. We're opening a post-incident ticket to PRD:INC-2245 for customer RCA.
Lee (oncall): Handoff: Alex, I'm going offline in 12m. Maria, can you take the lead when I step out? I'll leave runbook notes in the thread.
Maria G: Taking lead. I'll finish rule patch, push to staging, and roll to production if green. Also will file follow-up to add auto-batching cache gating to reduce VRAM pressure on cold-starts.
Samir: Action items:
- jen_ops: temp silence + drain jobs (done)
- Maria G: implement and test new alert rule + dashboard panels
- Alex M: coordinate customer comms & open RCA ticket
- Lee (oncall): add node-level watchlist and update handoff in runbook

Alex M: One more: add alertmanager grouping by node label `gpu_model` so we don't page for smaller T4-like nodes vs A100s. We should only page for high-density A100 racks.
Maria G: Agreed. I'll make the rule match `gpu_model=~"A100|H100"` for page severity.
jen_ops: Will also add a suppression that gates pages during planned draining windows (so the mitigation doesn't itself page).
Samir: Let's plan a short postmortem tomorrow 09:30 PT to review thresholds and rollout a "quiet hours" policy for non-customer-facing batch drains.
Alex M: Thanks all. Maria — please ping when the rule is live and paste the new alert URL. I'll notify customer success for the impacted tenants.
Maria G: Will do. :thumbsup:
inc-bot: Incident state changed: ACKNOWLEDGED by Maria G
Maria G: Update 15:04 UTC — new rule staged, dashboard panel added to incident board. Rolling to prod now.
jen_ops: Traffic shift complete, drained prod-rt-05/06. Observed p95 returning towards baseline on a few hosts.
Samir: Noted. Will add ticket to eng-sre backlog to evaluate long-term mitigations: smarter cache eviction, preforking, and smaller per-request memory caps.
Alex M: Closing loop: please add the exact alert rule text and the suppression window we used to the runbook before we call this resolved.
Maria G: Added to runbook and posted the alert URL: https://monitoring.redwood.ai/alerts/a-98324
Alex M: Great work. I'll file customer comms and mark this thread for the postmortem. :rocket:
